Event support: low (one official history, a passing reference; the date is the latest by which the party was there). current_activity: Corps command post at Grevenbroich, Germany; the corps is to take over the Rhine sector from Bonn to Neuss
notes: Event date: 28 March 1945 (History of the Fifteenth US Army, printed pp. 90-91 and 92-93: Letters of Instructions Numbers Thirteen and Fourteen, both dated 28 March 1945, list the corps command post in paragraph 5; Number Fourteen reads 'XXII Corps - Present: GREVENBROICH - Final: To be Reported'). Event definition: a command-post observation from the army's own orders, not a move; the corps (APO 250) is told to take over by 1 April the defense of the west bank of the Rhine from Bonn (exclusive) to Neuss (exclusive), and to be ready to occupy, organize and govern the Regierungsbezirke of Dusseldorf, Aachen and Koln. Relationship: Fifteenth Army assigned from 21 January 1945 (Wikipedia, Fifteenth Army, 'Subordinate units': XXII Corps 21 January 1945 to 20 January 1946; TheSecondWar.pl: the corps 'formally came under the army on 21 January 1945'); the start date comes from these two secondary accounts and no primary source read states it, while the army's orders of 28 March address the corps as a subordinate. Location: Grevenbroich (grid F1977 in the letters); the town centre stands for the command post and the grid reference was not plotted. Coordinates: Wikipedia (en): Grevenbroich. Commander: Maj. Gen. Ernest N. Harmon (The Supreme Command, appendix D, p. 540; Wikipedia, XXII Corps, gives his command from 23 January 1945 and TheSecondWar.pl from 14 January 1945 with 23 January as another listing; the day does not affect this row). Search: no source read places the corps headquarters between its stay at Doddington Hall (C0642) and this letter, so no claim is made for January to mid-March 1945. Event support: moderate (two letters of one date in one official history). Location support: moderate (named town in the army's order on the date; no second source for the place).

current_activity: Corps becomes operational and takes over the Rhine sector from Bonn to Neuss; 102nd, 95th and 86th Divisions in place
notes: Event date: 30 March 1945 (History of the Fifteenth US Army, p. 40: 'the mission assigned to the corps, which became operational 30 March 1945, provided for the defense of the west bank of the Rhine within its sector'; p. 46: the areas passed to the Fifteenth Army 'in four phases, during the period 30 March to 10 April', and the corps took operational control in place of the 102nd and 95th Infantry Divisions (both Ninth Army) and the 86th Infantry Division (First Army)). Event definition: the corps becomes operational and assumes the defense of the west bank of the Rhine from Bonn (exclusive) to Neuss (exclusive) (Letter of Instructions Thirteen, p. 90: by 1 April; extended to Homberg by 5 April, which is outside this batch). Ernest N. Harmon (see C0643). Event support: moderate (one official history states the date; no second source). Relationship: Fifteenth Army assigned (see C0643). The single corps column of the CMH tables does not say assigned or attached, so the corps relations of the 97th, 94th and 86th Divisions are unspecified subordination; the 95th, whose cell reads 'XXII (Opn)', is operational control; the 82d Airborne Division is attached, because the CMH Combat Chronicle (R565) words its entry of 31 March 1945 'First Allied (Abn) Army, but attached to the XXII Corps, Fifteenth Army, 12th Army Group' (the division stays assigned to the First Allied Airborne Army). The 102nd Division is not listed: its CMH table (R337) shows no XXII Corps row although the History says the corps took operational control of it in place (p. 46); no relation is recorded for it and the difference between the two sources is left open. Location: Grevenbroich, the nearest earlier command post (28 March, three days before the row; see C0643); the position on 31 March is not documented. Coordinates: Wikipedia (en): Grevenbroich.
